body { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0; background: #f6f7f9; color: #1d1f23; } .top { background: #1d4ed8; color: white; padding: 1rem 2rem; } main { max-width: 640px; margin: 2rem auto; display: grid; gap: 1.5rem; } .card { background: white; border-radius: 8px; padding: 1.25rem; box-shadow: 0 1px 3px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1); } form label { display: block; margin-top: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; } form input { width: 100%; padding: 0.5rem; box-sizing: border-box; } input:invalid { border: 2px solid #dc2626; background: #fef2f2; } .help-icon { display: inline-grid; place-items: center; width: 1.2em; height: 1.2em; border-radius: 50%; background: #e5e7eb; font-size: 0.8em; cursor: help; } #task-list { list-style: none; margin: 0; } #task-list li { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; padding: 0.5rem 0; border-bottom: 1px solid #eee; } button { cursor: pointer; } const list = document.getElementById('task-list'); const form = document.getElementById('add-form'); list.addEventListener('click', (event) => { const button = event.target.closest('button.delete'); if (!button) return; button.closest('li').remove(); }); form.addEventListener('submit', (event) => { event.preventDefault(); if (!form.checkValidity()) return; const title = form.elements.title.value.trim(); const li = document.createElement('li'); const id = String(Date.now()); li.dataset.id = id; li.innerHTML = ` `; li.querySelector('span').textContent = title; list.append(li); form.reset(); });

content.text:
The form no longer shows red errors when the page loads. A field only turns red after you've used it or tried to submit, and a short message under it says what's wrong. I haven't run it in a browser: I asked to run a syntax check (`node --check app.js`) and it was declined, so nothing has been tested.

**What I changed:**

- **`style.css`:** The red styling used to apply to any invalid field, including empty ones on load. Now it only applies once the script marks a field as having an error. I added a style for the red message line, and it keeps a fixed height so the form doesn't jump when a message appears.
- **`index.html`:** Each input now has a message line under it. Screen readers will read the message along with the field and announce it when it changes.
- **`app.js`:**
  - A field starts showing errors once you leave it or change its value. After that, the message updates as you type, so it disappears as soon as you fix the problem.
  - Clicking **Add task** shows errors on every field and moves the cursor to the first one that's wrong.
  - After a task is added, the form clears and goes back to showing no errors.

**The messages:**
- **Title:** "Enter a title for the task." or "Title must be at least 3 characters."
- **Owner email:** "Enter the owner's email address." or "Enter a valid email address, like name@example.com."
- **Due date:** "Choose a due date." or "Enter a complete, valid date."

I also made one change you didn't ask for: a title made only of spaces now counts as empty. Before, it would pass the browser's check and add a blank task.

To check it, open `index.html`. The form should load with no red. Click into Title and then out of it, and only Title should show an error. Click **Add task** with fields empty, and every empty field should show its message.
